subject: journey/ibnbattuta
prompt:
Create ONE landscape 3:2 historical field sketchbook page.
An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found. The traveller need not appear: some pages record only what the party saw (a harbour, a fortress, a market, an animal or plant). When the traveller does appear, draw them in action and in a natural, varied pose, not standing to attention. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect.
Scene: Granada circa1350, a closer architectural city view from a modest elevated Albaicin roof terrace across the narrow Darro ravine toward the Alhambra on the opposite Sabika hill. Major focus is the connected red-brown Nasrid fortification walls and blocky Alcazaba towers on the ridge, clearly grounded in the real topography, close enough to read masonry and wall rhythm. In lower foreground a diagonal cascade of tightly packed medieval houses: rough pale plaster, clay roof tiles, simple timber eaves, small enclosed courtyards and a fig tree, not a vast empty orchard. Trace of river far below, mountain slopes very lightly washed behind, no invented grand river bridge. An empty plain terracotta water jug at terrace edge establishes human viewing height; no protagonist. Daylight, restrained red ochre against faded grey-blue and dusty green. Do not show modern Granada, cathedral, Christian church towers, modern bell tower atop Torre de la Vela, flags, Charles V palace or later Court of Lions. Show a fourteenth-century fortification, not a fantasy castle or modern tourist panorama. Strong large-scale architectural observation and deep perspective, plenty of unfinished graphite edges and bare paper; no decorative border or lettering.
Use a clear distinctive viewpoint. Keep materials and clothing appropriate to the date. No writing, labels, captions, watermarks or signature.

edits.prompt: Edit this Granada sketchbook illustration, preserving the foreground Albaicin houses, terrace jug, aged paper, pencil and muted watercolour style. Correct only the Alhambra and its hillside: it should occupy a long, nearly level ridge, a connected low horizontal enclosure with the prominent plain rectangular Comares tower left of centre and the compact Alcazaba group at the western/right end. Remove the invented descending chain of freestanding tall towers and the enormous sheer cliff. Replace with a gentler wooded slope down to the Darro ravine. Make the fortress more restrained and architecturally credible, with broad plain rammed-earth walls, fewer narrow decorative windows and fewer castle-like crenellations. Keep the circa1350 Nasrid setting: no Charles V palace, cathedral, bell tower, flags, or later Christian buildings. Keep sky and mountains as faint unfinished pencil and pale washes, with more bare paper toward the upper edge. No writing or labels.

Make one precise historical correction to this image and preserve everything else: at the far right of the Alhambra skyline, the tallest rectangular tower has a tiny roofed bell turret sitting on top. REMOVE that entire small roofed belfry, its posts, roof and bell opening. Finish the main rectangular tower with an ordinary flat medieval parapet like the neighbouring square towers, with no rooftop structure, flags, crosses or bells. Keep every other part of the image unchanged: all houses, other towers, walls, hills, colour, pencil lines and paper.
